title: Nigeria History Tracker Update — May 09, 2026
summary: ISWAP launched coordinated back-to-back assaults on FOB Magumeri in Borno (May 7) and the 27 Brigade HQ in Yobe (May 9), killing four soldiers total and marking the most intense ISWAP offensive against fixed army installations in 2026. On the political front, Nigeria's opposition parties agreed to field a single presidential candidate for 2027, while the xenophobic killings of Nigerians in South Africa triggered a diplomatic standoff and House of Representatives resolution calling for sanctions. Economically, the naira stabilized near ₦1,374/$ with the IMF raising Nigeria's 2026 growth forecast to 4.1%, while the NLC led nationwide May Day protests demanding a minimum wage rise to ₦154,000 amid inflation of 15.38%. New map points added for the Plateau State conflict zone, FOB Magumeri, and the Yobe 27 Brigade area.
